subject: Technical runbook session planning & ML/infra attendees
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@avenbio.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@avenbio.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call earlier — super helpful to get an outside view on serving tradeoffs. A couple quick notes from our side:

- We're focused on lowering inference cost for our batch enrichment pipeline (avg seq len ~512) while keeping 95th pct latency under 200ms for interactive workflows.
- Data residency is a requirement for regulated patient data; we'll need to discuss private deployment options and audit logs.
- Key stakeholders: me (product), Priya Rao (ML lead), and our infra manager (TBD).

We'd like to move to a technical session next week to get the infra/ML team aligned — roughly 60–90 minutes to cover: architecture fit, LLM selection/quantization, KV cache strategy, and rollout plan. Can you suggest a couple of windows?

Best,
Emma
Emma Li
Senior Product Manager, AvenBio

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@avenbio.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@avenbio.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Emma — thanks for the clear summary and for looping Priya in.

Recap (very high level):
- Primary goal: reduce per-record inference cost for enrichment while preserving clinical-quality outputs for patient-facing features.
- Constraints: data residency + audit trails, predictable 95th pct latency for interactive checks.
- Success metric for the deep dive: a 1-page runbook with recommended model family, quantization level, batching strategy, and an initial rollout plan (canary + fallback).

Proposed next step: 60–90m technical runbook session with your ML + infra leads and our serving/ops engineers. Two windows that work for our ML/infra owners:

- Wednesday 2025-08-27, 09:30–11:00 PT (60–90m)
- Thursday 2025-08-28, 13:00–14:30 PT (60–90m)

Request for attendees from AvenBio: Priya (ML lead), your infra manager, and a product lead who is empowered to agree on rollout constraints. From Redwood: Karthik (serving runtime), Marcus (deployment/ops), and me.

Draft agenda (we'll refine):
1) 5m — goals & success criteria
2) 15–20m — current architecture + data residency constraints (AvenBio)
3) 20–25m — recommended serving topologies (dedicated vs private) & tradeoffs (Redwood)
4) 15m — batching/quantization options and expected unit-cost impact
5) 10–15m — rollout plan, metrics, and next actions (canary, monitoring)

I've attached a short prep doc that lists what we'll ask your team to bring (logs, sample p95/p99 latency, typical request volumes). If those windows don't fit, propose a couple of times and we'll iterate.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Looping in Marcus and adding a couple of pragmatic notes for the runbook session:

- If AvenBio's batch enrichment is tolerant of 1–2 token-level hallucination checks, we can optimize more aggressively with 4-bit quantization + prefix/KV caching. We'll want sample outputs to validate.
- For the session, please have: a) a small sample of 200 representative requests, b) p50/p95/p99 latencies, and c) an indication of peak QPS for enrichment runs.

Agenda tweak suggestion: add a 10-minute live demo of a fallback policy (how we fall back to a cheaper model variant under capacity pressure). That tends to answer operational questions quickly.

Happy to prep a short notebook to demonstrate quantization impact if Priya is ok with sharing a small model snapshot or a few tokens of representative text.

-Karthik
